The checksum is set to `SKIP`, which is common for VCS or dynamically generated downloads (such as those behind web forms or scripts), especially when the source is not a static, versioned file. The file operations are limited to creating directories, extracting files, moving them to the correct location, and setting standard permissions—none of which involve executing code, modifying system-wide configurations, or accessing sensitive user data.

The source URL points to a known domain associated with the AIMP ecosystem (`aimp.ru`), and the download is for a specific skin ID. There are no obfuscated commands, network exfiltration attempts, or unexpected system modifications. The package behaves as expected for a skin/theme package in the AUR.
</details>

This file contains no code, only metadata, and adheres to standard AUR packaging practices. While the source URL is not pinned to a specific commit or version and uses an unencrypted HTTP query, this is consistent with the upstream distribution model for AIMP skins. There is no evidence of obfuscation, unauthorized data exfiltration, or execution of remote code. The package appears to be a legitimate skin distribution.
